text:
Hi Benhur,

I have a question (well, few questions.. ) regarding DPs and FTR/FLs. Hope you don't mind me polluting your great journal.. :) Please consider the following example.

This is a USDCAD chart. I watched IF's decision points video over and over again. He says in the video that, price goes from one decision point to another. In the below H1 chart.. I have marked a DP which decides price is too expensive and then decides to go down the SR flip. IF shows that the decision is made at the open of the candle. (at least that's what I saw in the video).

1. But how do we really say that the decision is made at the open of the candle? when we go to LTFs, candle is narrowed down we can exactly find the LTF candle which broke the level. So the DP will be the opening point of the LTF candle.. Still if we have more and more LTFs.. we can further go down and narrow down. So which DP is the correct DP which decides the price is too expensive and broke the S/R flip level? DP1, DP2 or DP3?

2. Other thing is, If price is reacting to a DP, why would we need FTRs, FLs? In the example, the DP is different from the FTR. Price can react to the FTR or DP. Do we put our pending orders at FTR and Stoplosses on DPs ( in this example)?

3. Are FLs, FTRs new decision points made after the previous decision took place? ( For example, DP1 decided that price is too expensive and broke down the SR flip level and then made the new DP2)

Note: Price actually reacted to DP1. never reacted to the FTR.. I dont know why.

Thanks in advance.

author: benhur
text:
Hi VT

The moment when things clicked for me in my studies was the moment I realized nothing in the market is technical. Instead I started looking for places where I could find unfilled orders. Today, when I look at the chart I am searching for the ultimate bouncing levels, then I consider if I want to trade these levels.

At decision points there are unfilled orders and you can expect a bounce there. but be aware that a decision level is just the nearby barrier of a PAZ (price Action Zone). The further boundary of that PAZ can react too, because this is the first level that price was balanced with opposing orders, therefor just beyond it you can find unfilled orders. This is why you should consider FTR, FL, DP, CP, QM, DM - these all are variety of formations that unfold imbalanced order flow that you can use in your trading.

To make things more complex, yes you should drill down forever if possible to really fine your level. You should always remember that time is no factor of the market, therefore time frame is just a random necessity to document price. The events of the markets are documented by price only. So our job is harder to extract the finest level to act upon. Yes is no that straight forward, And yes we should be very happy it is like that, only the busy miners get reach the precious rocks.

To be more practical, do what I did for weeks during my initial learning phase; take two lines one for above price one for below market price. stare at one minute charts and place you lines where you know price will give a bounce. Do so for whole sessions with great patience and motivation to really see price in action. If you do so, come back and share with the RTM community your finding. I am sure there are going to be at least few priceless insights you take for life.

author: benhur
text:
I got this question in my PM, I think it worth to post my reply in public.

The question was related to my definition for Flag-Limits. as some of you know, I tend to breakdown everything to the OF arrays, by doing this I can assume where unfilled orders are located:Think of a Flag-Limit in terms of orderflow balance / imbalance.

The flag area show us where there was balanced OF, while the pole (the approach or the break) is where we assume to find imbalance.

We also assume that we can find unfilled orders where there was first (or last) imbalanced OF.

This, in theory explains the FL under and above.

The question wasWhen you said while the pole the approach or the break .. Do you mean the last H made inside a Flag before let's say price Engulfs down with LQ ? and by break you mean the Break of Support or Demand in the Flag ? also can't figure out exactly what do you mean by first or last Imbalanced ?

Here is an image to explain how FO aligned around FL

author: ViTaLDRuG
text:
Hi Benhur,

I noticed that, if a FL is broken, and then if another FL is created which hold the price up or down (It will hold the price up or down opposite to the direction the previous FL hold) and then the second FL is broken, that breaking swing will always go to the decision point there it was decided to break the first FL. Noticed this almost every time. In case of a perfect Flag (which has a big pole up/down), if its FL is broken, the price should go to the start of the pole. Of course the start of that pole should break another FL on the way to create the current Flag' FL.
